newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina groups to hold labour reform talks.
newsitem.headline: Argentina groups to hold labour reform talks.

text.p: Argentine government officials, businessmen and union leaders will meet in the next 48 hours to negotiate the government's labour reform project, the chief of the main union grouping, CGT, announced Tuesday.
"In 48 hours we will conduct a summit because it is fundamental to discuss the labour laws," said Rodolfo Daer of the CGT after meeting with a top governing Peronist Party lawmaker.

"It is important to create an atmosphere of dialogue with those who have the responsibility to lead the country," said Daer. Argentine Presidente Carlos Menem is seeking to pass more "flexible" labour laws to as a means to combat unemployment of 17.1 percent.
The package is staunchly opposed by unions on the grounds that it will allegedly undermine benefits for employees.
Jorge Matzkin, leader of the Peronist bloc in the Lower House of Congress, said after the meeting with Daer that "the meeting is necessary to find common ground."
